352|) -> InvestigationResult:
353|    """Run or continue an investigation (d5-pins.md pin 9)."""
354|    try:
355|        session = store.load(incident.id)
356|    except KeyError:
357|        session = None
358|    if session is None:
359|        session = Session(
360|            incident_id=incident.id,
361|            turn_limit=max_turns,
362|            read_limit=max_read_calls,
363|            token_limit=max_tokens,
364|            transcript_id=f"tx-{incident.id}",
365|            history=[
366|                {"role": "developer", "content": _read_prompt()},
367|                {
368|                    "role": "user",
369|                    "content": render_incident(
370|                        incident, tools.registry
371|                    ),
372|                },

376|        raise ValueError(

383|        session.read_limit = max_read_calls
384|        session.token_limit = max_tokens

389|def _open_segment(
390|    session: Session,
391|    *,
392|    message: str,
393|    extra_turns: int,
394|    extra_reads: int,
395|) -> None:
396|    """Start a new segment on a saved session (d5-pins 15, d6a-pins 1).
397|
398|    Shared by resume() and reopen(): budgets and counts reset, the turn
399|    is recorded so a later `none` needs evidence after it, and the
400|    message becomes the next user input.
401|    """
402|    session.segment_start_turn = session.turn
403|    session.turn_limit = session.turn + extra_turns
404|    session.read_limit = extra_reads
405|    session.segment_reads = 0
406|    session.segment_tokens = 0
407|    session.refused_submissions = 0
408|    session.resumed_at_turns.append(session.turn)
409|    session.status = "running"
410|    session.reason = ""
411|    session.history.append({"role": "user", "content": message})

162|    @classmethod
163|    def reconstruct(
164|        cls, incident_id: str, registry: Any, now: datetime
165|    ) -> "Incident":
166|        """Rebuild incident context from an incident ID and the registry.
167|
168|        The ToolSet reaches the gates through the session, which carries
169|        only the incident ID; the ID embeds service, environment,
170|        tripwire and trip time (pin 6), and the registry supplies the
171|        rest. Parsing matches the registry's known services,
172|        environments and tripwire IDs (longest first); it never splits
173|        on "-" because those names contain hyphens. Raises ValueError
174|        when the ID does not parse.
175|        """
176|        match = re.fullmatch(
177|            r"inc-(.+)-(\d{8}T\d{6}Z)", incident_id
178|        )
179|        if match is None:
180|            raise ValueError(f"bad incident id: {incident_id!r}")
181|        head, stamp = match.group(1), match.group(2)
182|        try:
183|            at = datetime.strptime(stamp, "%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ").replace(
184|                tzinfo=timezone.utc
185|            )
186|        except ValueError:
187|            raise ValueError(f"bad incident id: {incident_id!r}") from None
188|        found: tuple[str, str, str] | None = None
189|        services = sorted(registry.services, key=len, reverse=True)
190|        for service in services:
191|            prefix = f"{service}-"
192|            if not head.startswith(prefix):
193|                continue
194|            rest = head[len(prefix):]
195|            try:
196|                contract = registry.contract(service)
197|            except KeyError:
198|                continue
199|            tripwire_ids = {t.id for t in contract.tripwires}
200|            envs = sorted(
201|                {d.environment for d in registry.deployments(service)},
202|                key=len, reverse=True,

204|            for env in envs:

206|                if not rest.startswith(env_prefix):
207|                    continue
208|                tripwire_id = rest[len(env_prefix):]
209|                if tripwire_id in tripwire_ids:
210|                    found = (service, env, tripwire_id)
211|                    break
212|            if found is not None:

215|            raise ValueError(f"bad incident id: {incident_id!r}")

217|        deployment = f"{service}/{environment}"
218|        try:
219|            registry.deployment(deployment)
220|        except KeyError:
221|            raise ValueError(f"bad incident id: {incident_id!r}") from None
222|        event = SimpleNamespace(
223|            kind="trip",
224|            deployment=deployment,
225|            tripwire=tripwire_id,
226|            at=at,
227|            reason="",
228|            evidence=(),

233|def _resolve_param(value: Any, params: dict[str, Any]) -> Any:

236|    if isinstance(value, dict):

238|    if isinstance(value, list):

162|    @classmethod
163|    def reconstruct(
164|        cls, incident_id: str, registry: Any, now: datetime
165|    ) -> "Incident":
166|        """Rebuild incident context from an incident ID and the registry.
167|
168|        The ToolSet reaches the gates through the session, which carries
169|        only the incident ID; the ID embeds service, environment,
170|        tripwire and trip time (pin 6), and the registry supplies the
171|        rest. Parsing matches the registry's known services,
172|        environments and tripwire IDs (longest first); it never splits
173|        on "-" because those names contain hyphens. Raises ValueError
174|        when the ID does not parse.
175|        """
176|        match = re.fullmatch(
177|            r"inc-(.+)-(\d{8}T\d{6}Z)", incident_id
178|        )
179|        if match is None:
180|            raise ValueError(f"bad incident id: {incident_id!r}")
181|        head, stamp = match.group(1), match.group(2)
182|        try:
183|            at = datetime.strptime(stamp, "%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ").replace(
184|                tzinfo=timezone.utc
185|            )
186|        except ValueError:
187|            raise ValueError(f"bad incident id: {incident_id!r}") from None
188|        found: tuple[str, str, str] | None = None
189|        services = sorted(registry.services, key=len, reverse=True)
190|        for service in services:
191|            prefix = f"{service}-"
192|            if not head.startswith(prefix):
193|                continue
194|            rest = head[len(prefix):]
195|            try:
196|                contract = registry.contract(service)
197|            except KeyError:
198|                continue
199|            tripwire_ids = {t.id for t in contract.tripwires}
200|            envs = sorted(
201|                {d.environment for d in registry.deployments(service)},
202|                key=len, reverse=True,
203|            )
204|            for env in envs:
205|                env_prefix = f"{env}-"
206|                if not rest.startswith(env_prefix):
207|                    continue
208|                tripwire_id = rest[len(env_prefix):]
209|                if tripwire_id in tripwire_ids:
210|                    found = (service, env, tripwire_id)
211|                    break
212|            if found is not None:
213|                break
214|        if found is None:
215|            raise ValueError(f"bad incident id: {incident_id!r}")
216|        service, environment, tripwire_id = found
217|        deployment = f"{service}/{environment}"
218|        try:
219|            registry.deployment(deployment)
220|        except KeyError:
221|            raise ValueError(f"bad incident id: {incident_id!r}") from None
222|        event = SimpleNamespace(
223|            kind="trip",
224|            deployment=deployment,
225|            tripwire=tripwire_id,
226|            at=at,
227|            reason="",
228|            evidence=(),
229|        )
230|        return cls.from_trip(event, registry, now)

233|def _resolve_param(value: Any, params: dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
234|    if isinstance(value, str) and value.startswith("${") and value.endswith("}"):
235|        return params.get(value[2:-1], value)
236|    if isinstance(value, dict):
237|        return {k: _resolve_param(v, params) for k, v in value.items()}
238|    if isinstance(value, list):
239|        return [_resolve_param(v, params) for v in value]
240|    return value

"""Multi-act demo host (d8-pins 5). Holds one DemoRuntime at a time."""

import threading
from typing import Any


class DemoHost:
    """Holds one DemoRuntime; switch(name) builds and starts a fresh one."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        acts: dict[str, Any],
        *,
        live: bool = False,
        speed: float = 10.0,
        realtime: bool = False,
        turn_delay_s: float = 0.0,
    ) -> None:
        from fleetsre.demo.runtime import DemoRuntime  # noqa: F401

        self.acts = acts
        self.live = live
        self.speed = speed
        self.realtime = realtime
        self.turn_delay_s = float(turn_delay_s)
        self.current: Any = None
        self._stop: threading.Event | None = None
        self._thread: threading.Thread | None = None

    def switch(self, name: str) -> None:
        """Build and start a fresh runtime for the named act (d8-pins 5)."""
        from fleetsre.demo.runtime import DemoRuntime

        if name not in self.acts:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown act: {name}")
        self._stop_thread()
        runtime = DemoRuntime(
            self.acts[name], live=self.live, speed=self.speed,
            turn_delay_s=self.turn_delay_s,
        )
        runtime.act_name = name
        runtime.start()
        self.current = runtime
        if self.realtime:
            self._stop = threading.Event()
            self._thread = threading.Thread(
                target=runtime.run_realtime,
                args=(self._stop,),
                daemon=True,
            )
            self._thread.start()

    def stop(self) -> None:
        """Stop the realtime thread, if one is running."""
        self._stop_thread()

    def _stop_thread(self) -> None:
        if self._thread is not None:
            assert self._stop is not None
            self._stop.set()
            self._thread.join(timeout=5.0)
            self._thread = None
            self._stop = None

"""Multi-act demo host (d8-pins 5). Holds one DemoRuntime at a time."""

import threading
from typing import Any


class DemoHost:
    """Holds one DemoRuntime; switch(name) builds and starts a fresh one."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        acts: dict[str, Any],
        *,
        live: bool = False,
        speed: float = 10.0,
        realtime: bool = False,
        turn_delay_s: float = 0.0,
    ) -> None:
        from fleetsre.demo.runtime import DemoRuntime  # noqa: F401

        self.acts = acts
        self.live = live
        self.speed = speed
        self.realtime = realtime
        self.turn_delay_s = float(turn_delay_s)
        self.current: Any = None
        self._stop: threading.Event | None = None
        self._thread: threading.Thread | None = None

    def switch(self, name: str) -> None:
        """Build and start a fresh runtime for the named act (d8-pins 5)."""
        from fleetsre.demo.runtime import DemoRuntime

        if name not in self.acts:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown act: {name}")
        self._stop_thread()
        runtime = DemoRuntime(
            self.acts[name], live=self.live, speed=self.speed,
            turn_delay_s=self.turn_delay_s,
        )
        runtime.act_name = name
        runtime.start()
        self.current = runtime
        if self.realtime:
            self._stop = threading.Event()
            self._thread = threading.Thread(
                target=runtime.run_realtime,
                args=(self._stop,),
                daemon=True,
            )
            self._thread.start()

    def stop(self) -> None:
        """Stop the realtime thread, if one is running."""
        self._stop_thread()

    def _stop_thread(self) -> None:
        if self._thread is not None:
            assert self._stop is not None
            self._stop.set()
            self._thread.join(timeout=5.0)
            self._thread = None
            self._stop = None

import re

import pytest

from d8_helpers import (
    ADMIN_HEADERS,
    READ_TOOLS,
    drive,
    elide_encrypted,
    make_client,
    make_host,
    transcripts,
)


def _expected_segments(session):
    """Segment per turn: 1 plus resumes before the turn (d8-pins 14)."""
    resumes = sorted(session.resumed_at_turns)
    return {
        turn: 1 + sum(1 for r in resumes if r < turn)
        for turn in range(1, session.turn + 1)
    }


def test_d8_t9_turn_timeline():
    """D8-T9: one card per turn, exact inputs, divider, verdict classes.

    F1 at AWAITING_APPROVAL: the cards match the transcript records (think
    is the call's rationale, act is tool and args without it), and the
    header equals the sums over the records. Every turn's input equals the
    real transport request with encrypted_content elided. After F3's
    rejection reopen a divider shows trigger rejection. The HTML carries
    one card element per turn with the verdict as a CSS class.
    """
    from fleetsre.control.incidents import IncidentState

    host = make_host("F1")
    rt = host.current
    client = make_client(host)
    incident_id = rt.act.incident
    drive(rt, IncidentState.AWAITING_APPROVAL)

    response = client.get(f"/api/incidents/{incident_id}")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    view = response.json()
    records = transcripts(rt, incident_id)
    assert len(records) > 0
    turns = view["turns"]
    assert len(turns) == len(records)
    session = rt.store.load(incident_id)
    segments = _expected_segments(session)
    for card, record in zip(turns, records):
        assert card["n"] == record["turn"]
        assert card["segment"] == segments[record["turn"]]
        assert card["verdict"] == record["verdict"]
        assert card["usage"] == record["usage"]
        if record["tool"] is None:
            assert card["think"] == ""
        else:
            assert card["think"] == record["args"].get("rationale", "")
            assert card["act"] == {
                "tool": record["tool"],
                "args": {
                    k: v for k, v in record["args"].items()
                    if k != "rationale"
                },
            }
        if record["verdict"] == "refused":
            assert card["observe"]["problems"] == record["problems"]
            assert "error" in card["observe"]
        elif record["tool"] is not None:
            assert card["observe"] == record["output"]["result"]

    header = view["header"]
    assert header["turns"] == len(records)
    assert header["model_calls"] == len(records)
    assert header["read_calls"] == sum(
        1 for r in records
        if r["verdict"] == "accepted" and r["tool"] in READ_TOOLS
    )
    for key in (
        "input_tokens", "output_tokens", "reasoning_tokens", "cached_tokens",
    ):
        assert header["tokens"][key] == sum(r["usage"][key] for r in records)
    assert header["cost_usd"] == pytest.approx(
        sum(r["cost_usd"] for r in records)
    )
    expected_refusals: dict[str, int] = {}
    for record in records:
        if record["verdict"] == "refused":
            for problem in record["problems"]:
                rule = str(problem).split(":", 1)[0]
                expected_refusals[rule] = expected_refusals.get(rule, 0) + 1
    assert header["refusals"] == expected_refusals

    # Exact input: the real request, never a re-derivation (d8-pins §Review).
    requests = rt.transport.requests
    assert len(requests) == len(records)
    for card in turns:
        n = card["n"]
        got = client.get(f"/api/incidents/{incident_id}/turns/{n}/input")
        assert got.status_code == 200, n
        assert got.json() == elide_encrypted(requests[n - 1]["input"]), n

    # F3 after the rejection reopen: a divider with trigger rejection.
    host3 = make_host("F3")
    rt3 = host3.current
    client3 = make_client(host3)
    incident3 = rt3.act.incident
    drive(rt3, IncidentState.AWAITING_APPROVAL)
    proposal_hash = rt3.manager.get(incident3).proposals[-1].hash
    rejected = client3.post(
        f"/api/incidents/{incident3}/reject",
        json={
            "proposal_hash": proposal_hash,
            "notes": "unknown severities should map to 100",
        },
        headers=ADMIN_HEADERS,
    )
    assert rejected.status_code == 200
    rt3.advance(rt3.act.tick_seconds)
    assert rt3.manager.get(incident3).state == IncidentState.AWAITING_APPROVAL
    view3 = client3.get(f"/api/incidents/{incident3}").json()
    assert max(card["segment"] for card in view3["turns"]) == 2
    page3 = client3.get(f"/incidents/{incident3}")
    assert page3.status_code == 200
    assert re.search(
        r"segment-divider(.|\n){0,500}rejection", page3.text
    ), "no segment divider showing trigger rejection"

    # The HTML: one card element per turn, verdict as a CSS class.
    page = client.get(f"/incidents/{incident_id}")
    assert page.status_code == 200
    classes = [
        names.split()
        for names in re.findall(r'class="([^"]*)"', page.text)
        if "turn-card" in names.split()
    ]
    assert len(classes) == len(turns)
    got_verdicts = []
    for names in classes:
        verdicts = [v["verdict"] for v in turns]
        found = [name for name in names if name in verdicts]
        assert len(found) == 1, names
        got_verdicts.append(found[0])
    assert sorted(got_verdicts) == sorted(v["verdict"] for v in turns)

"""D8 acceptance: handoff card (d8-pins 15, Rows T10)."""

from d8_helpers import (
    ADMIN_HEADERS,
    ADMIN_TOKEN,
    drive,
    make_client,
    make_host,
    transcripts,
)


def _incident(client, incident_id):
    response = client.get(f"/api/incidents/{incident_id}")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    return response.json()


def _needs_input_f2():
    host = make_host("F2")
    rt = host.current
    client = make_client(host)
    from fleetsre.control.incidents import IncidentState

    drive(rt, IncidentState.NEEDS_INPUT)
    return host, rt, client


def test_d8_t10_handoff_card():
    """D8-T10: NEEDS_INPUT handoff, quiet wait, mark rotated, reply/grant/close.

    F2 at NEEDS_INPUT carries reason escalated, the session's hypotheses
    and evidence, a non-empty escalation summary, and the mark-rotated
    control in the admin HTML only. After 3600 s of quiet no model call
    was made. Clearing the credential_expiry fault resolves with action
    none. Fresh pauses: reply resumes without ticking, grant adds turns,
    close escalates with a postmortem.
    """
    from fleetsre.control.incidents import IncidentState

    host, rt, client = _needs_input_f2()
    incident_id = rt.act.incident
    view = _incident(client, incident_id)
    handoff = view["handoff"]
    assert handoff is not None
    assert handoff["reason"] == "escalated"
    session = rt.store.load(incident_id)
    assert [h["id"] for h in handoff["hypotheses"]] == list(session.hypotheses)
    assert len(handoff["evidence"]) == len(session.evidence)
    for item in handoff["evidence"]:
        recorded = session.evidence[item["id"]]
        assert item["hypothesis"] == recorded.hypothesis
        assert item["stance"] == recorded.stance
    record = rt.manager.get(incident_id)
    assert handoff["escalation_summary"] == (
        record.diagnosis["action"]["escalationSummary"]
    )
    assert handoff["escalation_summary"]
    last_refused = next(
        (r for r in reversed(transcripts(rt, incident_id))
         if r["verdict"] == "refused"),
        None,
    )
    if last_refused is None:
        assert handoff["last_refusal"] is None
    else:
        assert handoff["last_refusal"] == {
            "n": last_refused["turn"],
            "tool": last_refused["tool"],
            "problems": last_refused["problems"],
        }

    faults = rt.active_faults()
    assert len(faults) == 1
    assert faults[0]["type"] == "credential_expiry"
    assert faults[0]["environment"] == "bravo"
    clear_url = f"/api/demo/faults/{faults[0]['id']}/clear"
    admin_page = client.get(f"/incidents/{incident_id}?admin={ADMIN_TOKEN}")
    assert admin_page.status_code == 200
    assert clear_url in admin_page.text
    assert "mark rotated" in admin_page.text.lower()
    plain_page = make_client(host).get(f"/incidents/{incident_id}")
    assert plain_page.status_code == 200
    assert "/api/demo/faults/" not in plain_page.text
    assert "mark rotated" not in plain_page.text.lower()

    calls_before = rt.model_calls
    rt.advance(3600)
    assert rt.model_calls == calls_before
    assert rt.manager.get(incident_id).state == IncidentState.NEEDS_INPUT
    waiting = _incident(client, incident_id)
    assert waiting["handoff"]["model_calls_since_pause"] == 0

    cleared = client.post(clear_url, headers=ADMIN_HEADERS)
    assert cleared.status_code == 200
    assert all(
        f["id"] != faults[0]["id"] for f in rt.active_faults()
    )
    drive(rt, IncidentState.RESOLVED)
    assert rt.manager.get(incident_id).diagnosis["action"]["type"] == "none"

    _, rt_reply, client_reply = _needs_input_f2()
    incident_reply = rt_reply.act.incident
    tick_before = rt_reply.clock.now()
    reply = client_reply.post(
        f"/api/incidents/{incident_reply}/reply",
        json={"message": "rotated by hand"},
        headers=ADMIN_HEADERS,
    )
    assert reply.status_code == 200
    record_reply = rt_reply.manager.get(incident_reply)
    assert record_reply.state == IncidentState.INVESTIGATING
    assert record_reply.pending is not None
    assert record_reply.pending.message == (
        "Reply from operator: rotated by hand"
    )
    assert rt_reply.clock.now() == tick_before

    _, rt_grant, client_grant = _needs_input_f2()
    incident_grant = rt_grant.act.incident
    granted = client_grant.post(
        f"/api/incidents/{incident_grant}/grant",
        json={"turns": 4},
        headers=ADMIN_HEADERS,
    )
    assert granted.status_code == 200
    record_grant = rt_grant.manager.get(incident_grant)
    assert record_grant.state == IncidentState.INVESTIGATING
    assert record_grant.pending is not None
    assert record_grant.pending.extra_turns == 4

    _, rt_close, client_close = _needs_input_f2()
    incident_close = rt_close.act.incident
    closed = client_close.post(
        f"/api/incidents/{incident_close}/close",
        json={"note": "handing to netops"},
        headers=ADMIN_HEADERS,
    )
    assert closed.status_code == 200

import hashlib
import json
import secrets
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request, Response
from fastapi.responses import (
    HTMLResponse,
    JSONResponse,
    RedirectResponse,
)
from jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader

from fleetsre.web.views import fleet_view, incident_view, turn_input

TEMPLATES = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "templates"

_COOKIE = "fleetsre_admin"
_HEADER = "x-fleetsre-admin"


def _env() -> Environment:
    return Environment(
        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(TEMPLATES)), autoescape=True
    )


def _is_admin(request: Request, token: str) -> bool:
    candidates: list[str | None] = [
        request.headers.get("X-Fleetsre-Admin"),
        request.cookies.get(_COOKIE),
    ]
    for candidate in candidates:
        if candidate is None:
            continue
        try:
            if secrets.compare_digest(candidate, token):
                return True
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            continue
    return False


def _demo_view(host: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    rt = host.current
    last = rt.last_model_call_at
    transport = rt.transport
    names = sorted(host.acts.keys())
    return {
        "act": getattr(rt, "act_name", ""),
        "title": rt.act.title,

        "act_titles": {
            name: host.acts[name].title for name in names
        },
        "now": rt.clock.now().isoformat(),
        "started_at": rt.started_at.isoformat(),

        "active_faults": rt.active_faults(),

    }


def _version_view(host: Any) -> dict[str, str]:
    rt = host.current
    incidents = []
    for record in rt.manager.incidents():
        transcript_len = sum(

        )
        state = (
            record.state.value
            if hasattr(record.state, "value") else str(record.state)
        )
        incidents.append({
            "id": record.id,
            "state": state,
            "timeline": len(record.timeline),
            "transcript": transcript_len,
        })
    incidents.sort(key=lambda item: item["id"])
    payload = {
        "act": getattr(rt, "act_name", ""),
        "held": bool(rt.held),
        "incidents": incidents,
        "status": rt.evaluator.status(),
        "model_calls": rt.model_calls,

"""Demo web app (d8-pins 8-11). Admin-only local app with Jinja2 templates."""

import hashlib
import json
import secrets
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request, Response
from fastapi.responses import (
    HTMLResponse,
    JSONResponse,
    RedirectResponse,
)
from jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader

from fleetsre.web.views import fleet_view, incident_view, turn_input

TEMPLATES = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "templates"

_COOKIE = "fleetsre_admin"
_HEADER = "x-fleetsre-admin"


def _env() -> Environment:
    return Environment(
        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(TEMPLATES)), autoescape=True
    )


def _is_admin(request: Request, token: str) -> bool:
    candidates: list[str | None] = [
        request.headers.get("X-Fleetsre-Admin"),
        request.cookies.get(_COOKIE),
    ]
    for candidate in candidates:
        if candidate is None:
            continue
        try:
            if secrets.compare_digest(candidate, token):
                return True
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            continue
    return False


def _demo_view(host: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    rt = host.current
    last = rt.last_model_call_at
    transport = rt.transport
    names = sorted(host.acts.keys())
    return {
        "act": getattr(rt, "act_name", ""),
        "title": rt.act.title,
        "acts": names,
        "act_titles": {
            name: host.acts[name].title for name in names
        },
        "now": rt.clock.now().isoformat(),
        "started_at": rt.started_at.isoformat(),
        "speed": rt.speed,
        "held": bool(rt.held),
        "model_calls": rt.model_calls,
        "last_model_call_at": last.isoformat() if last else None,
        "active_faults": rt.active_faults(),
        "exhausted": bool(
            transport.exhausted if transport is not None else False
        ),
        "live": bool(getattr(host, "live", False)),
        "model": rt.gateway.config.roles["investigate"].model,
    }


def _version_view(host: Any) -> dict[str, str]:
    rt = host.current
    incidents = []
    for record in rt.manager.incidents():
        transcript_len = sum(
            len(rt.store.transcript(tid)) for tid in record.transcript_ids
        )
        state = (
            record.state.value
            if hasattr(record.state, "value") else str(record.state)
        )
        incidents.append({
            "id": record.id,
            "state": state,
            "timeline": len(record.timeline),
            "transcript": transcript_len,
        })
    incidents.sort(key=lambda item: item["id"])
    payload = {
        "act": getattr(rt, "act_name", ""),
        "held": bool(rt.held),
        "incidents": incidents,
        "status": rt.evaluator.status(),
        "model_calls": rt.model_calls,
    }
    canonical = json.dumps(
        payload, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")
    ).encode("utf-8")
    return {"version": hashlib.sha1(canonical).hexdigest()}


def create_app(
    host: Any, *, admin_token: str, operator: str = "operator"
) -> FastAPI:
    """Build the admin-only app: grid, incident, timeline, handoff (d8-pins 8)."""
    app = FastAPI()
    templates = _env()

    def _grid_page(request: Request) -> Response:
        query_token = request.query_params.get("admin")
        admin_error = False
        if query_token is not None:
            try:
                ok = secrets.compare_digest(query_token, admin_token)
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                ok = False
            if ok:
                response = RedirectResponse(url="/", status_code=302)
                response.set_cookie(
                    _COOKIE, admin_token, httponly=True,
                    samesite="strict", path="/",
                )
                return response
            admin_error = True
        admin = _is_admin(request, admin_token)
        rt = host.current
        with rt.lock:
            fleet = fleet_view(rt)
            demo = _demo_view(host)
        html = templates.get_template("grid.html").render(
            fleet=fleet, demo=demo, admin=admin,
            admin_error=admin_error,
        )
        return HTMLResponse(html)

    def _incident_page(
        request: Request, incident_id: str
    ) -> Response:
        query_token = request.query_params.get("admin")
        admin_error = False
        if query_token is not None:
            try:
                ok = secrets.compare_digest(query_token, admin_token)
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                ok = False
            if ok:
                response = RedirectResponse(
                    url=f"/incidents/{incident_id}", status_code=302
                )
                response.set_cookie(
                    _COOKIE, admin_token, httponly=True,
                    samesite="strict", path="/",
                )
                return response
            admin_error = True
        admin = _is_admin(request, admin_token)
        rt = host.current
        with rt.lock:
            try:
                view = incident_view(rt, incident_id)
            except (ValueError, KeyError):
                demo = _demo_view(host)
                html = templates.get_template("not_found.html").render(
                    demo=demo, admin=admin,
                    admin_error=admin_error,
                    incident_id=incident_id,
                )
                return HTMLResponse(html, status_code=404)
            demo = _demo_view(host)
            environment = view["deployment"].split("/", 1)[-1]
            rotatable = [
                fault for fault in rt.active_faults()
                if fault["type"] == "credential_expiry"
                and fault["environment"] == environment
            ]
        html = templates.get_template("incident.html").render(
            view=view, demo=demo, admin=admin, rotatable=rotatable,
            admin_error=admin_error,
        )
        return HTMLResponse(html)

    @app.get("/")
    def _get_grid(request: Request) -> Response:
        return _grid_page(request)

    @app.get("/api/fleet")
    def _get_fleet() -> dict[str, Any]:
        rt = host.current
        with rt.lock:
            return fleet_view(rt)

    @app.get("/incidents/{incident_id}")
    def _get_incident_page(
        request: Request, incident_id: str
    ) -> Response:
        return _incident_page(request, incident_id)

"""D8 acceptance: fleet grid (d8-pins 12, Rows T1)."""

from d8_helpers import drive, make_client, make_host


def test_d8_t1_fleet_grid():
    """D8-T1: /api/fleet covers every armed deployment with evaluator health.

    After start(), every registry deployment is listed with every component
    and tripwire, each status equal to evaluator.status(); the HTML holds
    every deployment ID. Driven to F1's first trip, alpha's connector and
    deployment are tripped with the act's incident, and the rest are ok.
    """
    from fleetsre.control.incidents import IncidentState

    host = make_host("F1")
    rt = host.current
    client = make_client(host)

    response = client.get("/api/fleet")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    fleet = response.json()
    assert fleet["act"] == "F1"
    expected_ids = [d.id for d in rt.evaluator.deployments]
    got_ids = [
        d["id"] for service in fleet["services"] for d in service["deployments"]
    ]
    assert got_ids == expected_ids

    status = rt.evaluator.status()
    contract = rt.registry.contract("alert-ingestion")
    by_component: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for tripwire in contract.tripwires:
        by_component.setdefault(tripwire.component, []).append(tripwire.id)
    kinds = {c.id: c.kind for c in contract.components}
    for service in fleet["services"]:
        for deployment in service["deployments"]:
            assert deployment["incident"] is None
            assert deployment["health"] == "ok"
            got_components = {
                c["id"]: c for c in deployment["components"]
            }
            assert set(got_components) == set(by_component)
            for comp_id, comp in got_components.items():
                assert comp["kind"] == kinds[comp_id]
                assert comp["health"] == "ok"
                got_tw = {t["id"]: t["status"] for t in comp["tripwires"]}
                assert set(got_tw) == set(by_component[comp_id])
                for tw_id, tw_status in got_tw.items():
                    assert tw_status == status[deployment["id"]][tw_id]

    page = client.get("/")
    assert page.status_code == 200
    for deployment_id in expected_ids:
        assert deployment_id in page.text

    drive(rt, IncidentState.AWAITING_APPROVAL)
    fleet = client.get("/api/fleet").json()
    by_id = {
        d["id"]: d
        for service in fleet["services"]
        for d in service["deployments"]
    }
    alpha = by_id["alert-ingestion/alpha"]
    assert alpha["health"] == "tripped"
    connector = next(
        c for c in alpha["components"] if c["id"] == "connector"
    )
    assert connector["health"] == "tripped"
    assert alpha["incident"] is not None
    assert alpha["incident"]["id"] == rt.act.incident
    assert alpha["incident"]["state"] == "AWAITING_APPROVAL"
    for deployment_id, deployment in by_id.items():
        if deployment_id != "alert-ingestion/alpha":
            assert deployment["health"] == "ok", deployment_id
            assert deployment["incident"] is None, deployment_id

# D8 pins

Interfaces and semantics for D8 (minimal): `deliverables.md` §D8 rows T1, T2, T3, T6, T8, T9 and T10. Written before the tests PR. **This file wins over the §D8 rows, goal and interface block where they differ**, including the text the 2026-11-01 re-plan made stale:
- there is no URL for judges;
- there is no `ChaosLoop` and no public mode;
- T8 links only the repo and the video.

North star: a working `make demo` that carries the video's F1, F2 and F3 beats with no surprises.

## Scope

- **In:**
  - a demo runtime that plays one act (F1, F2 or F3) at a time, each in the world its D6 scripted segments were generated in;
  - a local web app (admin only) with these pages: the grid, the incident view, the turn timeline and the handoff card;
  - approve, reject, reply, grant turns and close, plus one demo control: "mark rotated";
  - `make demo` and `make demo-check`;
  - the README's required structure (T8).
- **Out:**
  - public mode, the chaos loop and any deployed instance;
  - step mode;
  - persistence;
  - live streaming of turns while a segment runs;
  - intel-sync acts;
  - authoring in the UI (the authoring beat is a recorded `make author` run).
- **Who writes what:**
  - Muse writes all code and tests, and `fixtures/demo/acts.yaml` in Session A, from P1.
  - Claude drafts the README; Rixon commits it (pin 20).
- **No new model surface.** Scripted by default. With `MODEL_API_KEY` set, the investigate role is live (pin 6).

## Why acts

Each `fixtures/scripted/d6/<fault>.json` was generated in its own world: that fault's seed, t0 and schedule, with the canary scheduler on (d6a pin 23). Incident IDs depend on the first trip, and the scripts cite global `insertId`s. Running F1, F2 and F3 in one world would break all of this:
- the insertIds would shift, and `record_evidence` would refuse them;
- one `ScriptedTransport` list cannot route responses to incidents;
- F3's trip on alpha would attach to F1's open incident (d6a pin 10).

So `make demo` plays **one act at a time**, each a replica of its D6 end-to-end test world, behind one UI. Switching acts starts a fresh world.

## Interfaces

1. **`fixtures/demo/acts.yaml`** (Session A, from P1; protected once merged). One entry per act, keyed `F1`, `F2`, `F3`:
   ```yaml
   F1:
     title: "Connector stall on alpha"
     seed: <int>
     t0: "<ISO 8601 Z>"
     tick_seconds: 15
     faults:                       # exactly the D6 E2E schedule (D4 semantics 1)
       - { at: <s>, type: connector_stall, environment: alpha }
     responses:                    # scripted segment files, concatenated in this order
       - fixtures/scripted/d6/F1.json
     incident: "<expected incident ID>"
     actions:                      # what --check does; the human does these in the video
       - { on: AWAITING_APPROVAL, do: approve }
   ```
   - `do` ∈ {`approve`, `reject` (with `notes`), `mark_rotated`}. `on` is the incident state that enables the action.
   - Actions run in list order, each at most once.
   - F2: `[{on: NEEDS_INPUT, do: mark_rotated}]`.
   - F3: `[{on: AWAITING_APPROVAL, do: reject, notes: "unknown severities should map to 100"}, {on: AWAITING_APPROVAL, do: approve}]`, with responses `F3-reject` then `F3-revise`, or whatever P1 finds the D6-T17 test used.

2. **`fleetsre/demo/acts.py`.** `ActSpec` (pydantic, `extra="forbid"`) mirrors pin 1. `load_acts(path="fixtures/demo/acts.yaml") -> dict[str, ActSpec]`.

3. **`fleetsre/demo/transport.py`.** `DemoTransport(responses: list[dict])`:
   - It wraps `ScriptedTransport` and accepts `timeout`.
   - When the script is used up, it sets `exhausted = True` and raises `TransportError(400)`. Under d5-pins 17 that becomes `needs_input`/`model_unavailable` at once, with no backoff sleeps.
   - `calls: int` counts every `create`.

4. **`fleetsre/demo/runtime.py`.** `DemoRuntime(act: ActSpec, *, live: bool = False, speed: float = 10.0, lead_s: int = 60)` builds what the D6 end-to-end tests build:
   - a seeded `World` on a `MemorySink` and a `SimClock` at `t0`, with the act's faults scheduled through `world.schedule`;
   - the `Evaluator`, `CanaryScheduler` and `Registry`;
   - an obs-reader `ToolSet` (gates on), a `MemorySessionStore` and an `Investigator`;
   - an `ApprovalStore`, an `Executor` (deployer), a `Verifier` and an `IncidentManager`;
   - a `ControlLoop`;
   - the mock Chronicle app, reached in-process exactly as in d6a pin 22.

   Members:
   - Attributes `act`, `clock`, `world`, `sink`, `evaluator`, `registry`, `manager`, `store` and `loop`. `transport` is the `DemoTransport` in scripted mode, or `None` when live.
   - `lock: threading.RLock`. Every member below, and every web handler, holds it.
   - `start()` runs `loop.step()` synchronously until `first_fault_at − lead_s`, where `first_fault_at = t0 + min(fault.at)`. It records that instant as `started_at`.
   - `advance(seconds)` calls `loop.step()` until the clock has moved `seconds`, holding the clock while needed (pin 9).
   - `run_realtime(stop: threading.Event)` runs `advance(tick_seconds)` every `tick_seconds / speed` real seconds until `stop` is set.
   - `active_faults() -> list[dict]` returns the world's active faults (`id`, `type`, `environment`), by the same `World` method the `/_chaos/faults` routes use.
   - `clear_fault(fault_id)` calls `world.clear(fault_id)` and appends a `demo` timeline event `{"action": "mark_rotated", "fault": fault_id}` to the open incident on that environment, if there is one.
   - `model_calls` and `last_model_call_at` (sim time). They are counted by a wrapper on the transport, which works in live mode too.
   - `held: bool` (pin 9).

5. **`fleetsre/demo/host.py`.** `DemoHost(acts: dict[str, ActSpec], *, live=False, speed=10.0)`:
   - `current: DemoRuntime`;
   - `switch(name)` builds and `start()`s a fresh runtime, stops the realtime thread if one is running, and starts a new one only if `realtime=True` was passed to the constructor. Tests construct it without the thread.

6. **Live mode.** With `MODEL_API_KEY` set and `--live` passed, the investigate role uses `OpenAITransport` exactly as d5-pins 10 builds it, and `responses` are ignored.
   - `--check` refuses `--live` (exit 2), so CI and `make demo-check` never spend money.
   - Without `--live`, a key in the environment is ignored, so a demo never spends money unless asked. This narrows T6's "scripted model unless a key is set".

7. **`python -m fleetsre.demo`.**
   - Options: `[--act F1] [--host 127.0.0.1] [--port 8000] [--speed 10] [--live]` or `--check [--delay S ...]`.
   - **Serve:** it builds a `DemoHost`, starts the act, and serves `create_app` with uvicorn on `127.0.0.1`. It prints `Admin: http://127.0.0.1:<port>/?admin=<token>` and `Act: <name> — <title>`.
   - **`--check`:** for every act and every `--delay` (default `0 600 1800`), headless:
     - start the act;
     - `advance` one tick at a time, at most 4 simulated hours;
     - perform each action in `actions` when its `on` state is reached, plus `delay` simulated seconds for actions on `NEEDS_INPUT` (pin 9: the clock is held in AWAITING_APPROVAL, so delay does not apply there);
     - stop when the act's incident is RESOLVED or ESCALATED, or at the cap.

     It prints one line per run: `ACT {"act","delay","incident","state","modelCalls","scriptLength","exhausted","refusals","firstTripAt","resolvedAt"}`, with times as offsets from t0 in seconds. It exits 0 iff every run ends RESOLVED, with `incident` equal to the act's, `modelCalls == scriptLength` and `exhausted` false. Otherwise it exits 1.
   - **Makefile:**
     - `make demo` is `python -m fleetsre.demo --act $(ACT)`, with `ACT ?= F1`. It replaces the D0 placeholder.
     - `make demo-check` is `python -m fleetsre.demo --check`.
     - `make check` does not run `demo-check`; T6 covers it.

8. **`fleetsre/web/app.py`.**
   - `create_app(host: DemoHost, *, admin_token: str, operator: str = "operator") -> FastAPI`.
   - The token comes from `FLEETSRE_ADMIN_TOKEN`, or else `secrets.token_urlsafe(16)` at start.
   - Templates are Jinja2 under `fleetsre/web/templates/`, with inline CSS and a little vanilla JS. There is no build step, no framework and no CDN.
   - View data comes from pure functions in `fleetsre/web/views.py`: `fleet_view(rt)`, `incident_view(rt, id)` and `turn_input(rt, id, turn)`. The routes return them as JSON and render them as HTML.

## Semantics

9. **Clock hold.** While the act's incident is AWAITING_APPROVAL, `advance` does not step the loop and `held` is true; the header shows "clock held: awaiting approval".
   - Approval timing then cannot change what the scripted segments see: the reopen after a rejection and the apply after an approval run on the next tick, as in D6-T6, T8 and T17.
   - NEEDS_INPUT does not hold the clock. F2's quiet wait is real simulated time: the canary attaches, and no model call is made.
   - This is the honest framing for the video: "the demo clock waits for the approver".

10. **Routes.** An unknown incident gets 404, and a `ValueError` from the manager gets 409 `{"error": str}`.

    | Method | Path | Admin | Does |
    | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    | GET | `/` | no | Grid page (T1) |
    | GET | `/api/fleet` | no | `fleet_view` (pin 12) |
    | GET | `/incidents/{id}` | no | Incident page: view, timeline, handoff card (T2, T9, T10) |
    | GET | `/api/incidents` | no | `[{id, deployment, state, reason, opened_at}]` |
    | GET | `/api/incidents/{id}` | no | `incident_view` (pins 13–15) |
    | GET | `/api/incidents/{id}/turns/{n}/input` | no | `turn_input` (pin 14) |
    | GET | `/api/demo` | no | `{act, title, acts, now, started_at, speed, held, model_calls, last_model_call_at, active_faults, exhausted, live}` |
    | GET | `/api/version` | no | `{version}`, pin 17 |
    | POST | `/api/incidents/{id}/approve` | yes | `{proposal_hash}` → `manager.approve(..., by=operator)` |
    | POST | `/api/incidents/{id}/reject` | yes | `{proposal_hash, notes}` → `manager.reject(..., by=operator, notes=...)` |
    | POST | `/api/incidents/{id}/reply` | yes | `{message, extra_turns=0}` → `manager.reply` |
    | POST | `/api/incidents/{id}/grant` | yes | `{turns}` (1–24) → `manager.reply(id, f"Granted {turns} more turns.", by=operator, extra_turns=turns)` |
    | POST | `/api/incidents/{id}/close` | yes | `{note}` → `manager.close` |
    | POST | `/api/demo/faults/{fault_id}/clear` | yes | `rt.clear_fault` ("mark rotated"); 404 if the fault isn't active |
    | POST | `/api/demo/act` | yes | `{act}` → `host.switch` |

    Bodies are JSON, sent by `fetch`, so no form parsing is needed. Every POST returns the updated `incident_view`, or `/api/demo` for the demo routes.

11. **Admin credential.**
    - `GET` any page with `?admin=<token>`. A correct token sets the cookie `fleetsre_admin=<token>` (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Path=/) and redirects to the same path without the query. A wrong one is ignored.
    - A POST is admin when the cookie or an `X-Fleetsre-Admin` header matches the token, compared with `secrets.compare_digest`. Otherwise it gets 403 `{"error": "admin credential required"}` and nothing changes.
    - Pages render action controls only for an admin request. A non-admin page is the read-only view.

12. **Grid (T1).** `fleet_view` returns:
    ```
    {"act", "now", "held", "services": [{"service", "deployments": [{"id", "environment", "health",
       "incident": {"id", "state"} | null,
       "components": [{"id", "kind", "health", "tripwires": [{"id", "status"}]}]}]}]}
    ```
    - It covers every deployment the act's registry arms, in registry order.
    - A tripwire's `status` is `evaluator.status()[deployment][tripwire]`. A component is `tripped` if any of its tripwires is, and a deployment if any component is; otherwise `ok`.
    - `incident` is the deployment's latest incident.
    - The HTML has one row per deployment and one cell per component, coloured by health, with the incident linked. The header shows the act, the sim time, `held`, the model-call count with the last call's sim time, and active faults.

13. **Incident view (T2).** `incident_view` returns:
    - `id`, `deployment`, `state`, `reason`, `tripwires`, `timeline` (`record.timeline`), and `postmortem` (`model_dump(mode="json")` or `null`).
    - `hypotheses`: from `store.load(id)`, with `id`, `statement`, `wouldConfirm` and `alternative`.
    - `evidence`: one item per recorded `Evidence`, with `id`, `hypothesis`, `stance`, `why` and `recordedAtTurn`, plus `source`:
      - a log source becomes `{"kind": "log", "insertId", "timestamp", "severity", "event", "message", "deployment"}`, resolved through the act's `LogQuery.get`;
      - a tool source becomes `{"kind": "toolResult", "callId", "tool", "field", "value"}`, with `tool` from `session.calls[callId]`.
    - `diagnosis`: `record.diagnosis` or `null`. `category` is shown prominently.
    - `proposal`: the latest proposal or `null`, with `hash`, `seq`, `method`, `resource`, `update_mask` and `diff`.
      - `diff` is a list of `{field, before, after}`. For `parameters`, there is one row per proposed `displayName`, with field `parameters[<displayName>]`. Other masked fields get one row each.
      - `before` comes from `Proposal.resource_before` (pin 18). A `PASSWORD` value shows as `********`.
      - `*.restart` and `*.runOnDemand` have an empty `diff` and a `steps` summary (`enabled: false → true`, or `run once`).
    - `verification`: `null` until a `verification_started` event. Then `{tripwire, seconds, started_at, deadline, current, outcome}`, where:
      - `current` is the target's status from `evaluator.status()`;
      - `outcome` is `pending`, or `verified` or `failed` from the latest such timeline event.

      The web layer never calls `verifier.check`. The manager owns transitions.
    - `turns`, `header` and `handoff` (pins 14–15).
    - The HTML shows all of these: hypotheses with their evidence under them, the diff as a before → after table, the verification line and the postmortem when present.

14. **Turn timeline (T9).**
    - **`turns`:** one card per transcript record (d5-pins 18), across every `transcript_id` of the record, in order:
      - `n`, the session turn;
      - `segment`: 1, plus the number of resumes before this turn;
      - `think`, the call's `rationale` (`""` if there is no tool call);
      - `act`: `{tool, args}` with `rationale` removed;
      - `observe`: the tool result, or `{error, problems}` for a refusal;
      - `verdict`, and `usage`.
    - **Colour by verdict:** `accepted` green, `refused` red, `wouldRefuse` amber, and `no_tool_call` and `stuck` grey.
    - A segment divider precedes the first card of each segment after the first, showing the `resumed` event's trigger and message.
    - **`header`:**
      - `turns` and `model_calls`: the number of records;
      - `read_calls`: accepted calls to the eight read tools;
      - `tokens`: summed `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `reasoning_tokens` and `cached_tokens`;
      - `cost_usd`;
      - `refusals`: refused records' problems counted by rule, the text before the first `:`.
    - **Exact input (`turn_input`).** The input of turn `n` is `[developer: prompts/investigate.md, user: render_incident(...)] + history[:i]`, where:
      - `history` is the saved `Session.history`;
      - `i` is the index of turn `n`'s first output item in `history`, found by dict equality and searching forward from turn `n−1`'s index.

      Every `encrypted_content` value is replaced with `"<encrypted: N chars>"`. Nothing else is changed, the last-turn and resume messages included. This needs no change to D5's transcript.
    - **Expansion.** A card's `<details>` loads `turn_input` on open and shows the items as indented JSON, with the developer prompt collapsed.

15. **Handoff card (T10).**
    - `handoff` is `null` unless the state is NEEDS_INPUT. Otherwise it has:
      - `reason`;
      - `hypotheses` and `evidence`, as in pin 13;
      - `last_refusal`: the last refused record's `{n, tool, problems}`, or `null`;
      - `escalation_summary`, from `record.diagnosis.action.escalationSummary` when the reason is `escalated`;
      - `paused_at`;
      - `model_calls_since_pause`: model calls made after `paused_at`, which the F2 beat shows as 0.
    - **Admin controls:**
      - reply, with a message and optional extra turns;
      - grant turns;
      - close, with a note;
      - **mark rotated**, shown only when `active_faults()` has a `credential_expiry` on the incident's environment. It posts that fault's ID to the clear route.
    - After mark rotated, the incident stays NEEDS_INPUT until the evaluator sees a tripped tripwire go `ok`. Then it resumes by d6a pin 13, which is what the video shows.

16. **Script exhaustion.**
    - If the human leaves the act's path, the next model call raises `TransportError(400)`, the incident pauses `needs_input`/`model_unavailable`, and `/api/demo` shows `exhausted: true`.
    - The header then shows "script ended: switch act to restart". Leaving the path means, for example, approving F3's `-1` proposal, or replying to F2 instead of marking it rotated.
    - Nothing crashes.

17. **Refresh.**
    - `/api/version` is the SHA-1 of the canonical JSON of: act, `held`, each incident's (id, state, timeline length, transcript length), `evaluator.status()` and `model_calls`.
    - Each page polls it every 2 s and reloads when it changes, unless a `<details>` is open. Then it shows "updated: reload" instead.
    - Sim time alone does not change the version.

"""D8 acceptance: fleet grid (d8-pins 12, Rows T1)."""

from d8_helpers import drive, make_client, make_host


def test_d8_t1_fleet_grid():
    """D8-T1: /api/fleet covers every armed deployment with evaluator health.

    After start(), every registry deployment is listed with every component
    and tripwire, each status equal to evaluator.status(); the HTML holds
    every deployment ID. Driven to F1's first trip, alpha's connector and
    deployment are tripped with the act's incident, and the rest are ok.
    """
    from fleetsre.control.incidents import IncidentState

    host = make_host("F1")
    rt = host.current
    client = make_client(host)

    response = client.get("/api/fleet")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    fleet = response.json()
    assert fleet["act"] == "F1"
    expected_ids = [d.id for d in rt.evaluator.deployments]
    got_ids = [
        d["id"] for service in fleet["services"] for d in service["deployments"]
    ]
    assert got_ids == expected_ids

    status = rt.evaluator.status()
    contract = rt.registry.contract("alert-ingestion")
    by_component: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for tripwire in contract.tripwires:
        by_component.setdefault(tripwire.component, []).append(tripwire.id)
    kinds = {c.id: c.kind for c in contract.components}
    for service in fleet["services"]:
        for deployment in service["deployments"]:
            assert deployment["incident"] is None
            assert deployment["health"] == "ok"
            got_components = {
                c["id"]: c for c in deployment["components"]
            }
            assert set(got_components) == set(by_component)
            for comp_id, comp in got_components.items():
                assert comp["kind"] == kinds[comp_id]
                assert comp["health"] == "ok"
                got_tw = {t["id"]: t["status"] for t in comp["tripwires"]}
                assert set(got_tw) == set(by_component[comp_id])
                for tw_id, tw_status in got_tw.items():
                    assert tw_status == status[deployment["id"]][tw_id]

    page = client.get("/")
    assert page.status_code == 200
    for deployment_id in expected_ids:
        assert deployment_id in page.text

    drive(rt, IncidentState.AWAITING_APPROVAL)
    fleet = client.get("/api/fleet").json()
    by_id = {
        d["id"]: d
        for service in fleet["services"]
        for d in service["deployments"]
    }
    alpha = by_id["alert-ingestion/alpha"]
    assert alpha["health"] == "tripped"
    connector = next(
        c for c in alpha["components"] if c["id"] == "connector"
    )
    assert connector["health"] == "tripped"
    assert alpha["incident"] is not None
    assert alpha["incident"]["id"] == rt.act.incident
    assert alpha["incident"]["state"] == "AWAITING_APPROVAL"
    for deployment_id, deployment in by_id.items():
        if deployment_id != "alert-ingestion/alpha":
            assert deployment["health"] == "ok", deployment_id
            assert deployment["incident"] is None, deployment_id

# D8 pins

Interfaces and semantics for D8 (minimal): `deliverables.md` §D8 rows T1, T2, T3, T6, T8, T9 and T10. Written before the tests PR. **This file wins over the §D8 rows, goal and interface block where they differ**, including the text the 2026-11-01 re-plan made stale:
- there is no URL for judges;
- there is no `ChaosLoop` and no public mode;
- T8 links only the repo and the video.

North star: a working `make demo` that carries the video's F1, F2 and F3 beats with no surprises.

## Scope

- **In:**
  - a demo runtime that plays one act (F1, F2 or F3) at a time, each in the world its D6 scripted segments were generated in;
  - a local web app (admin only) with these pages: the grid, the incident view, the turn timeline and the handoff card;
  - approve, reject, reply, grant turns and close, plus one demo control: "mark rotated";
  - `make demo` and `make demo-check`;
  - the README's required structure (T8).
- **Out:**
  - public mode, the chaos loop and any deployed instance;
  - step mode;
  - persistence;
  - live streaming of turns while a segment runs;
  - intel-sync acts;
  - authoring in the UI (the authoring beat is a recorded `make author` run).
- **Who writes what:**
  - Muse writes all code and tests, and `fixtures/demo/acts.yaml` in Session A, from P1.
  - Claude drafts the README; Rixon commits it (pin 20).
- **No new model surface.** Scripted by default. With `MODEL_API_KEY` set, the investigate role is live (pin 6).

## Why acts

Each `fixtures/scripted/d6/<fault>.json` was generated in its own world: that fault's seed, t0 and schedule, with the canary scheduler on (d6a pin 23). Incident IDs depend on the first trip, and the scripts cite global `insertId`s. Running F1, F2 and F3 in one world would break all of this:
- the insertIds would shift, and `record_evidence` would refuse them;
- one `ScriptedTransport` list cannot route responses to incidents;
- F3's trip on alpha would attach to F1's open incident (d6a pin 10).

So `make demo` plays **one act at a time**, each a replica of its D6 end-to-end test world, behind one UI. Switching acts starts a fresh world.

## Interfaces

1. **`fixtures/demo/acts.yaml`** (Session A, from P1; protected once merged). One entry per act, keyed `F1`, `F2`, `F3`:
   ```yaml
   F1:
     title: "Connector stall on alpha"
     seed: <int>
     t0: "<ISO 8601 Z>"
     tick_seconds: 15
     faults:                       # exactly the D6 E2E schedule (D4 semantics 1)
       - { at: <s>, type: connector_stall, environment: alpha }
     responses:                    # scripted segment files, concatenated in this order
       - fixtures/scripted/d6/F1.json
     incident: "<expected incident ID>"
     actions:                      # what --check does; the human does these in the video
       - { on: AWAITING_APPROVAL, do: approve }
   ```
   - `do` ∈ {`approve`, `reject` (with `notes`), `mark_rotated`}. `on` is the incident state that enables the action.
   - Actions run in list order, each at most once.
   - F2: `[{on: NEEDS_INPUT, do: mark_rotated}]`.
   - F3: `[{on: AWAITING_APPROVAL, do: reject, notes: "unknown severities should map to 100"}, {on: AWAITING_APPROVAL, do: approve}]`, with responses `F3-reject` then `F3-revise`, or whatever P1 finds the D6-T17 test used.

2. **`fleetsre/demo/acts.py`.** `ActSpec` (pydantic, `extra="forbid"`) mirrors pin 1. `load_acts(path="fixtures/demo/acts.yaml") -> dict[str, ActSpec]`.

3. **`fleetsre/demo/transport.py`.** `DemoTransport(responses: list[dict])`:
   - It wraps `ScriptedTransport` and accepts `timeout`.
   - When the script is used up, it sets `exhausted = True` and raises `TransportError(400)`. Under d5-pins 17 that becomes `needs_input`/`model_unavailable` at once, with no backoff sleeps.
   - `calls: int` counts every `create`.

4. **`fleetsre/demo/runtime.py`.** `DemoRuntime(act: ActSpec, *, live: bool = False, speed: float = 10.0, lead_s: int = 60)` builds what the D6 end-to-end tests build:
   - a seeded `World` on a `MemorySink` and a `SimClock` at `t0`, with the act's faults scheduled through `world.schedule`;
   - the `Evaluator`, `CanaryScheduler` and `Registry`;
   - an obs-reader `ToolSet` (gates on), a `MemorySessionStore` and an `Investigator`;
   - an `ApprovalStore`, an `Executor` (deployer), a `Verifier` and an `IncidentManager`;
   - a `ControlLoop`;
   - the mock Chronicle app, reached in-process exactly as in d6a pin 22.

   Members:
   - Attributes `act`, `clock`, `world`, `sink`, `evaluator`, `registry`, `manager`, `store` and `loop`. `transport` is the `DemoTransport` in scripted mode, or `None` when live.
   - `lock: threading.RLock`. Every member below, and every web handler, holds it.
   - `start()` runs `loop.step()` synchronously until `first_fault_at − lead_s`, where `first_fault_at = t0 + min(fault.at)`. It records that instant as `started_at`.
   - `advance(seconds)` calls `loop.step()` until the clock has moved `seconds`, holding the clock while needed (pin 9).
   - `run_realtime(stop: threading.Event)` runs `advance(tick_seconds)` every `tick_seconds / speed` real seconds until `stop` is set.
   - `active_faults() -> list[dict]` returns the world's active faults (`id`, `type`, `environment`), by the same `World` method the `/_chaos/faults` routes use.

   - `held: bool` (pin 9).

5. **`fleetsre/demo/host.py`.** `DemoHost(acts: dict[str, ActSpec], *, live=False, speed=10.0)`:

   - Without `--live`, a key in the environment is ignored, so a demo never spends money unless asked. This narrows T6's "scripted model unless a key is set".

It exits 0 iff every run ends RESOLVED, with `incident` equal to the act's, `modelCalls == scriptLength` and `exhausted` false. Otherwise it exits 1.

8. **`fleetsre/web/app.py`.**
   - `create_app(host: DemoHost, *, admin_token: str, operator: str = "operator") -> FastAPI`.

## Semantics

9. **Clock hold.** While the act's incident is AWAITING_APPROVAL, `advance` does not step the loop and `held` is true; the header shows "clock held: awaiting approval".

    - A tripwire's `status` is `evaluator.status()[deployment][tripwire]`. A component is `tripped` if any of its tripwires is, and a deployment if any component is; otherwise `ok`.

      - `think`, the call's `rationale` (`""` if there is no tool call);
      - `act`: `{tool, args}` with `rationale` removed;
      - `observe`: the tool result, or `{error, problems}` for a refusal;
      - `verdict`, and `usage`.
    - **Colour by verdict:** `accepted` green, `refused` red, `wouldRefuse` amber, and `no_tool_call` and `stuck` grey.
    - A segment divider precedes the first card of each segment after the first, showing the `resumed` event's trigger and message.
    - **`header`:**
      - `turns` and `model_calls`: the number of records;
      - `read_calls`: accepted calls to the eight read tools;
      - `tokens`: summed `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `reasoning_tokens` and `cached_tokens`;
      - `cost_usd`;
      - `refusals`: refused records' problems counted by rule, the text before the first `:`.
    - **Exact input (`turn_input`).** The input of turn `n` is `[developer: prompts/investigate.md, user: render_incident(...)] + history[:i]`, where:
      - `history` is the saved `Session.history`;
      - `i` is the index of turn `n`'s first output item in `history`, found by dict equality and searching forward from turn `n−1`'s index.

    - **Expansion.** A card's `<details>` loads `turn_input` on open and shows the items as indented JSON, with the developer prompt collapsed.

15. **Handoff card (T10).**
    - `handoff` is `null` unless the state is NEEDS_INPUT. Otherwise it has:
      - `reason`;
      - `hypotheses` and `evidence`, as in pin 13;
      - `last_refusal`: the last refused record's `{n, tool, problems}`, or `null`;
      - `escalation_summary`, from `record.diagnosis.action.escalationSummary` when the reason is `escalated`;
      - `paused_at`;
      - `model_calls_since_pause`: model calls made after `paused_at`, which the F2 beat shows as 0.
    - **Admin controls:**
      - reply, with a message and optional extra turns;
      - grant turns;
      - close, with a note;
      - **mark rotated**, shown only when `active_faults()` has a `credential_expiry` on the incident's environment. It posts that fault's ID to the clear route.
    - After mark rotated, the incident stays NEEDS_INPUT until the evaluator sees a tripped tripwire go `ok`. Then it resumes by d6a pin 13, which is what the video shows.

    - If the human leaves the act's path, the next model call raises `TransportError(400)`, the incident pauses `needs_input`/`model_unavailable`, and `/api/demo` shows `exhausted: true`.
    - The header then shows "script ended: switch act to restart". Leaving the path means, for example, approving F3's `-1` proposal, or replying to F2 instead of marking it rotated.
    - Nothing crashes.

    - `/api/version` is the SHA-1 of the canonical JSON of: act, `held`, each incident's (id, state, timeline length, transcript length), `evaluator.status()` and `model_calls`.

    - Sim time alone does not change the version.

    - The app binds to 127.0.0.1 only.

    - Claude drafts `README.md` after Session B. Rixon commits it to `impl/d8` before that PR merges. Session B does not create or edit `README.md`, so T8 is red until then.

      - **Gates** names every gate rule family: `order`, `hypotheses`, `evidence`, `diagnosis`, `reads.cap`.

    - `escalation_summary` is non-empty;
    - the mark-rotated control is in the admin HTML and not in the non-admin HTML.

10|class DemoTransport:

13|
14|    def __init__(
15|        self, responses: list[dict[str, Any]], *, turn_delay_s: float = 0.0
16|    ) -> None:

18|        self._script_length = len(responses)
19|        self.exhausted = False
20|        self.calls = 0
21|        self._turn_delay_s = float(turn_delay_s)
22|
23|    @property
24|    def requests(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
25|        return self._inner.requests
26|

28|    def timeouts(self) -> list[float]:
29|        return self._inner.timeouts
30|
31|    @property
32|    def script_length(self) -> int:
33|        return self._script_length
34|
35|    def create(
36|        self, request: dict[str, Any], *, timeout: float = 120.0
37|    ) -> dict[str, Any]:

39|        self.calls += 1
40|        try:
41|            response = self._inner.create(request, timeout=timeout)

def _seq(entries):
    return [(entry["actor"], entry["kind"]) for entry in entries]


def test_f1_awaiting_next_and_story():

    rt = host.current
    record = drive(rt, IncidentState.AWAITING_APPROVAL)

    entries = story(rt, record)
    assert _seq(entries) == [
        ("tripwire", "opened"),
        ("sre", "proposal"),
    ]
    assert "no connector.run.completed" in entries[0]["text"]
    assert entries[1]["text"].startswith(
        "SRE (scripted replay) investigated \u00b7 9 turns"
    )

    diagnosis = proposal.diagnosis
    assert diagnosis["category"] in entries[1]["text"]
    assert diagnosis["summary"] in entries[1]["text"]
    assert proposal.method in entries[1]["text"]
    for entry in entries:
        assert "mark rotated" not in entry["text"].lower()


def test_f2_needs_before_and_after_clear():
    host = make_host("F2")
    rt = host.current
    record = drive(rt, IncidentState.NEEDS_INPUT)
    step = next_step(rt, record)
    assert step["actor"] == "you"
    diagnosis = record.diagnosis
    assert step["text"] == (
        "The SRE found credential failure on bravo "
        f"({diagnosis['summary']}). "
        "The fix is outside what the SRE may do. "
        f"{diagnosis['action']['escalationSummary']}"
    )
    entries = story(rt, record)
    assert _seq(entries) == [
        ("tripwire", "opened"),
        ("sre", "needs_input"),
    ]
    assert entries[1]["text"].startswith(
        "SRE (scripted replay) investigated \u00b7 9 turns"
    )
    assert "escalated" in entries[1]["text"]
    assert record.diagnosis["action"]["escalationSummary"] in entries[1]["text"]

    fault_id = rt.active_faults()[0]["id"]
    rt.clear_fault(fault_id)
    cleared = rt.manager.get(rt.act.incident)
    demo_detail = [
        event.detail for event in cleared.timeline if event.kind == "demo"
    ][0]
    assert demo_detail["by"] == "operator"

    assert "credential rotated at" in step["text"]
    assert "to recover, then the SRE resumes" in step["text"]
    assert "connector-errors" in step["text"]
    entries = story(rt, cleared)
    assert _seq(entries) == [
        ("tripwire", "opened"),
        ("sre", "needs_input"),
        ("you", "demo"),
    ]
    assert entries[2]["text"] == "rotated the credential outside the platform"
    for entry in entries:
        assert "mark rotated" not in entry["text"].lower()


def test_f2_resolved_next_and_story():
    host = make_host("F2")
    rt = host.current
    drive(rt, IncidentState.NEEDS_INPUT)
    rt.clear_fault(rt.active_faults()[0]["id"])
    record = drive(rt, IncidentState.RESOLVED)
    step = next_step(rt, record)
    assert step["actor"] == "done"
    assert step["text"].startswith("RESOLVED at ")
    entries = story(rt, record)
    assert _seq(entries) == [
        ("tripwire", "opened"),
        ("sre", "needs_input"),
        ("you", "demo"),
        ("tripwire", "recovery"),
        ("sre", "segment"),
        ("platform", "verification_started"),
        ("tripwire", "verified"),
    ]
    sre_entries = [entry for entry in entries if entry["actor"] == "sre"]
    assert len(sre_entries) == 2
    first, second = sre_entries
    assert first["text"].startswith(
        "SRE (scripted replay) investigated \u00b7 9 turns"
    )
    assert "Fix is outside the allowlist; needs a human." in first["text"]
    assert second["text"].startswith(
        "SRE resumed after the tripwire recovered"
    )
    assert "Re-checked" in second["text"]
    assert record.postmortem.closed_at.strftime("%H:%M:%S") in step["text"]
    assert record.postmortem.closed_at.isoformat() not in step["text"]
    for entry in entries:
        assert "mark rotated" not in entry["text"].lower()

def test_f3_rejection_notes_verbatim_and_revise():
    host = make_host("F3")
    rt = host.current
    client = make_client(host)
    drive(rt, IncidentState.AWAITING_APPROVAL)
    notes = "unknown severities should map to 100"
    proposal_hash = rt.manager.get(rt.act.incident).proposals[-1].hash
    rejected = client.post(
        f"/api/incidents/{rt.act.incident}/reject",
        json={"proposal_hash": proposal_hash, "notes": notes},
        headers=ADMIN_HEADERS,
    )
    assert rejected.status_code == 200
    rt.advance(rt.act.tick_seconds)
    record = rt.manager.get(rt.act.incident)
    assert record.state == IncidentState.AWAITING_APPROVAL
    entries = story(rt, record)
    assert _seq(entries) == [
        ("tripwire", "opened"),
        ("sre", "proposal"),
        ("you", "rejected"),
        ("sre", "proposal"),
    ]
    assert notes in entries[2]["text"]
    assert entries[3]["text"].startswith("SRE resumed after your rejection")
    first = record.proposals[0].diagnosis["summary"]
    second = record.proposals[1].diagnosis["summary"]
    assert first != second
    assert first in entries[1]["text"]
    assert second in entries[3]["text"]
    assert notes in entries[2]["text"]
    for entry in entries:
        assert "mark rotated" not in entry["text"].lower()


def test_queued_reply_shows():
    host = make_host("F2")
    rt = host.current
    client = make_client(host)
    drive(rt, IncidentState.NEEDS_INPUT)
    message = "rotated by hand"
    reply = client.post(
        f"/api/incidents/{rt.act.incident}/reply",
        json={"message": message},
        headers=ADMIN_HEADERS,
    )
    assert reply.status_code == 200
    record = rt.manager.get(rt.act.incident)
    assert record.state == IncidentState.INVESTIGATING
    step = next_step(rt, record)
    assert step == {
        "actor": "sre", "text": "resumes on the next tick: reply",
    }
    entries = story(rt, record)
    assert _seq(entries) == [
        ("tripwire", "opened"),
        ("sre", "needs_input"),
        ("you", "reply"),
    ]
    queued = entries[-1]
    assert queued["actor"] == "you"
    assert message in queued["text"]
    assert "queued; the SRE resumes on the next tick" in queued["text"]

def test_inline_script_passes_node_check():
    node = shutil.which("node")
    if node is None:
        return
    host = make_host("F1")
    rt = host.current
    client = make_client(host)
    drive(rt, IncidentState.AWAITING_APPROVAL)
    page = client.get(
        f"/incidents/{rt.act.incident}?admin={ADMIN_TOKEN}"
    ).text
    scripts = re.findall(r"<script>(.*?)</script>", page, re.DOTALL)
    assert scripts
    for script in scripts:
        if not script.strip():
            continue
        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(
            "w", suffix=".js", delete=False
        ) as handle:
            handle.write(script)
            name = handle.name
        try:
            proc = subprocess.run(
                [node, "--check", name],
                capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30,
            )
        finally:
            Path(name).unlink(missing_ok=True)
        assert proc.returncode == 0, proc.stderr


def test_f2_segments_use_their_own_diagnoses_and_disjoint_evidence():
    host = make_host("F2")
    rt = host.current
    drive(rt, IncidentState.NEEDS_INPUT)
    rt.clear_fault(rt.active_faults()[0]["id"])
    record = drive(rt, IncidentState.RESOLVED)
    entries = story(rt, record)
    sre_entries = [entry for entry in entries if entry["actor"] == "sre"]
    assert len(sre_entries) == 2
    first, second = sre_entries
    seg1_summary = "The bravo connector credential expired; upstream 401s."
    seg2_summary = (
        "The bravo connector credential had expired; rotation restored it."
    )
    assert seg1_summary in first["text"]
    assert "Fix is outside the allowlist; needs a human." in first["text"]
    assert seg2_summary not in first["text"]
    assert second["text"].startswith(
        "SRE resumed after the tripwire recovered"
    )
    assert "Re-checked" in second["text"]
    assert seg2_summary in second["text"]
    first_ids = {item["id"] for item in first["evidence"]}
    second_ids = {item["id"] for item in second["evidence"]}
    assert first_ids == {"E1", "E2", "E3"}
    assert second_ids == {"E4"}
    assert first_ids.isdisjoint(second_ids)

def test_live_config_fails_fast_on_hung_call():
    from fleetsre.demo.runtime import _live_config
    from fleetsre.sre.gateway import (
        GatewayConfig,
        ModelGateway,
        RoleConfig,
        TransportError,
    )

    config = _live_config()
    role = config.roles["investigate"]
    assert role.timeout_s == 60
    assert role.retry_timeouts is False

    class _HungTransport:
        def __init__(self) -> None:
            self.calls = 0

        def create(self, request, *, timeout):
            self.calls += 1
            assert timeout == 60
            raise TransportError(504, "timed out", timeout=True)

    hung = _HungTransport()
    slept: list[float] = []
    gateway = ModelGateway(
        GatewayConfig(
            roles={"investigate": RoleConfig(
                model="m", reasoning_effort="low",
                timeout_s=60, retry_timeouts=False,
            )},
            base_url="https://x",
            max_retries=5,
        ),
        hung,
        sleep=slept.append,
    )
    try:
        gateway.respond("investigate", [], None)
    except TransportError as exc:
        assert exc.timeout is True
    else:
        raise AssertionError("hung call should raise")
    assert hung.calls == 1
    assert slept == []

    attempts = {"count": 0}

    class _FlakyTransport:
        def create(self, request, *, timeout):
            attempts["count"] += 1
            if attempts["count"] == 1:
                raise TransportError(429, "rate limited")
            return {"output": [], "usage": {}}

    slept2: list[float] = []
    gateway2 = ModelGateway(
        GatewayConfig(
            roles={"investigate": RoleConfig(
                model="m", reasoning_effort="low",
                timeout_s=60, retry_timeouts=False,
            )},
            base_url="https://x",
            max_retries=5,
        ),
        _FlakyTransport(),
        sleep=slept2.append,
    )
    gateway2.respond("investigate", [], None)
    assert attempts["count"] == 2
    assert slept2 == [1.0]
